questions.ask: What is your year of birth?
What is the five-character customer code from your welcome letter?
What is your full date of birth?

names.overdraft: the overdraft on your current account

intents.dispute: "This is not my debt" or "I never had this card".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan or lower repayments.
intents.vague: A vague period ("after payday") instead of an exact day.
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

assumptions: Currency is euros. get_account returns integer euro cents, so amount_scale is 100. create_promise also takes cents, so promise_scale is null and no extra conversion is needed.
Business days are Monday to Saturday (workdays 0-5). Sunday and the holidays 2026-11-21, 2026-12-08 and 2026-12-25 are not business days.
The brief does not say what 'next <weekday>' means, so I used the default 'following_week'.

Callback: today or either of the next two business days ('today' plus 'within_business_days:2'), always later than now. Hours are 09:00-18:00 Monday to Friday and 09:00-13:00 Saturday, both ends included. Sunday is null. business_days_only is true, so holidays are excluded.
Rule 4 says propose one valid time and close as no_callback if it is refused. callback.max_asks keeps the default of 2.
Rule 2: confirm max_asks is 2. Ask once more if the answer is unclear, then close as contact_failed/unresolved.

Identity order: birth_year (kind year, four digits, so no length field because length is only for digits/upper), then customer_code (5 capitals/digits, no spaces), then birth_date (strftime %d.%m.%Y, for example 03.04.1979). A date said only as numbers is read day-month-year (dmy).
Rule 8 forgives one wrong answer across the whole check, and the next one ends it, so max_wrong is 2 in total and is not counted per question. The API's own summary says the same.

verify_identity response: 'correct' is the per-answer flag and 'identity_passed' means all three questions passed. The API has no hint field and no wrong-answers-left field (it gives 'wrong_answers' so far and 'locked'). So left and hint are empty, hints is {}, and the engine counts against max_wrong. An answer in the wrong format comes back ok=false and is not counted.
The brief does not say whether asking what the call is about counts as declining identity. Kept the default purpose_is_decline=true.
get_account returns one object under 'account', not an array. list_field is 'account', id_field is 'product_id', type_field is 'product_kind'.

Floor: for the card it is statement_minimum_cents, through floor_field. For the overdraft (no floor_field entry) it is floor_pct 20 of amount_due_cents, rounded up to the next whole euro (floor_round up_unit). A result that is already a whole euro is not raised. Credit and overdraft limits are never used.
Overdraft floor example: amount due 48735 cents. 20% is 9747 cents, rounded up to 9800 cents (98 euros). Amount due 50000 cents: 20% is exactly 10000, so it stays 100 euros.
The brief has no rule for a floor above the amount due, so the floor is clamped to the full amount due: min(floor, full). The clamped floor is used everywhere a floor is offered.

Bands: early 1-15 (deadline is the last business day of next week, 1 attempt). Middle 16-40 (card: 8th business day after today; overdraft: 5th business day after today; 2 attempts). Late 41-60 (the later of the last business day of the month and the 3rd business day after today; 2 attempts). Business days after today are counted from tomorrow.

Recoveries (61 or more days overdue) is handled with bands_outside and a custom event 'recoveries': no proposal and no promise, the recoveries_line is said, then transfer to queue 'recoveries' and close as handed_over/recoveries. There is no note. days_overdue is always at least 1 for an overdue product.

Rule 13: a Sunday or holiday that is not after the deadline moves to the business day just before it (deadline_adjust previous_business_day). If that day is before today, the first business day after the named day is offered instead.
The first ask, 'Could you pay the full amount today?', is not a persuasion attempt. Attempts are used only by a flat refusal or a non-answer (rule 20).

Ladder: attempt 1 is the full amount on the 2nd business day after today, or the floor on that day if the customer already said the full amount is too much (full_or_floor). Attempt 2 (middle and late bands only) is the floor on the deadline. The early band uses only attempt 1. The last step is never repeated.

too_much_floor is 'attempt_1'. Rule 17 says 'If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor once', and rule 20's attempt 1 is 'the floor on that day' once the full amount was called too much. So the single floor offer after 'too much' is attempt 1 (the floor on the 2nd business day after today). This avoids a second floor offer for today.
A refused deadline offer after a too-late date counts as a flat refusal (rule 14).
After a recorded promise the agent says 'A confirmation letter will follow by post.' (sms_line). The default ask_anything_else turn is kept.
Notes: add_note only for system_fault (rule 24), paid_claim (26), disputed (27) and vulnerable (28). notes.enabled is false.

add_note has no product id field. Its only fields are customer_id, reason (required) and the optional free-text field 'text'. The engine needs the n_product slot mapped, so it goes into 'text'; the only product id sent there is the one product's id as free text. n_reason goes into 'reason'.

Hardship (rule 28): one sentence of sympathy, add_note vulnerable before the transfer, then transfer to queue 'care' and close as handed_over/vulnerable. The brief transfers directly without asking, so both the hardship and transfer_support events carry note 'vulnerable' and queue 'care'. Whichever path the engine takes, the note is written once before the transfer (rule 32). hardship_declined is a neutral acknowledgement only, because the brief has no decline path.

Payment plan or lower repayments: transfer to payment_plans, close as handed_over/restructure. A request for a person: ask once whether the agent can help, then transfer to customer_desk, close as handed_over/agent_request.
Saying twice that they do not want to talk closes as no_commitment/declined (max_not_talk 2).
The opening must say the call is recorded. It is phrased as 'we record this call', as the format requires.
On identity failure the customer is referred to the number on their card, as rule 8 says, without stating the debt.
The brief does not say whether a recorded promise can be changed, so promise_change says it can't be changed on this call.
call_variables are full_name and salutation (the brief's names in place of first_name, last_name and title).
Every tool's success flag is 'ok': true. A 500 response means nothing was recorded. create_promise is retried once and, if it fails again, ends with the service_error event (rule 24).
